passed: Root identifiers and the version-specific citation DOI are reconciled by version_access.
The human-subjects declaration is accompanied by ethics review and informed consent.
Participant and recording totals agree across description and instances; smaller feature counts are compatible with the disclosed feature-generation omissions.
Registered feature access and more restrictive raw-audio access are consistent across licensing, raw_sources and data_governance.
The selected NIH grant and documented purpose align with the funding description.
Version 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 release dates are ordered consistently, and issued matches the 1.1.0 release date.
Documented distribution formats agree with the file inventory and the exclusion of original voice recordings from this release.
warnings: Collection-to-processing-to-publication chronology cannot be fully assessed because collection timeframes are missing.
The cited b2aiprep version is explicitly not confirmed as the version executed for this release.
Some pediatric protections and voice-risk statements originate in a wider-study protocol, limiting release-specific verification.

correctness_validations.doi_format: Valid textual DOI formats: 10.13026/mf9s-5r03 and 10.13026/h995-bt35 use the PhysioNet prefix. Resolution was not checked.
correctness_validations.grant_number_format: The selected 3OT2OD032720-01S1 identifier has a valid NIH supplemental-award structure. Caveated alternative identifiers were not treated as the pediatric award.
correctness_validations.rrid_format: RRID:SCR_007345 has valid software/resource RRID syntax in the citation; it was not treated as a dataset-specific identifier.
correctness_validations.url_validity: Documented HTTPS URLs have plausible structures and repository or project domains. Live reachability was not checked.

issues_detected.description: The record documents ethics approval, consent, pediatric protections and privacy precautions, but lacks comprehensive release-specific deidentification and privacy-impact documentation and compensation status. The broader protocol's voice-risk statement does not complete an assessment of released derived features.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document the safeguards and residual-risk assessment applicable to the released pediatric features, the relevant data protection framework, and compensation status. Distinguish release-specific evidence from wider-study procedures.

issues_detected.description: Access authorization and the DACO contact are clear, but substantive reuse obligations, intellectual-property restrictions and an explicit confidentiality classification are not documented.
issues_detected.recommendation: Summarize the applicable agreement obligations, regulatory requirements and confidentiality classification, retaining the existing distinction between registered feature access and controlled raw-audio access.

issues_detected.description: Standard formats, dictionaries, identifiers and a BIDS processing step are described, but the release's schema conformance and integration mapping are not specified sufficiently to establish the highest interoperability band.
issues_detected.recommendation: Identify the schema or standard versions governing the released files and document identifier scope, join relationships and an integration procedure across feature, phenotype and metadata files.

issues_detected.description: The software citation does not establish the b2aiprep version used for this release, and executed versions for other named tools are missing. Feature failures and quality handling are described only partially.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record executed software versions or commits, reproducible workflow settings, relevant quality assessments and explicit handling of failed or missing features.

issues_detected.description: Detailed collection mechanisms are not accompanied by collection date ranges or explicit descriptions of the personnel or roles performing collection.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add the collection timeframe and collector roles or qualifications, distinguishing these from investigator affiliations and release dates.

issues_detected.description: Release history and persistent repository access are documented, but maintenance ownership, update policy and long-term preservation commitments are unspecified.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the maintenance contact, describe update and correction procedures, and state the preservation arrangements or institutional commitment.

issues_detected.description: Intended research and screening uses are listed without prohibited or discouraged uses or a social-impact analysis connecting risks to mitigations.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document supported-use boundaries, inappropriate uses and downstream risks with mitigation guidance, including limitations relevant to pediatric screening and clinical interpretation.

issues_detected.description: Version history and general transformations do not provide complete relationships among identified source entities, processing activities, responsible agents and released outputs.
issues_detected.recommendation: Provide textual or structured lineage linking source versions, processing steps and responsible agents to output artifacts, with explicit exclusions and missing-feature derivations.

issues_detected.description: The record does not analyze known biases or effects on intended uses. Single-site recruitment, language eligibility, non-verbal exclusion, microphone selection and feature failures are documented as facts without a corresponding bias or fairness discussion.
issues_detected.recommendation: Assess the effects of sampling, language and communication coverage, recording equipment and feature missingness on intended uses. Document supported findings, limitations, mitigations and fairness analyses, using a standard taxonomy where appropriate.

semantic_insights: The record explicitly separates pediatric evidence from adult-dataset facts and qualifies wider-study protocol statements.
The latest-version DOI and version-specific DOI are distinguished, resolving an apparent identifier discrepancy.
Released derived features and controlled raw audio have clearly differentiated access routes and authorization requirements.
Feature dimensions and extraction parameters provide useful technical detail without establishing full processing provenance.
Pediatric consent and assent descriptions are substantial and retain their source-scope limitations.
The complete root record is the sole scoring unit; file collections do not become separately scored datasets, and observed record facts do not replace independent applicability declarations.
